messages:
Lee (Support): Customer reported an incorrect tool call: their integration asked for a balance check but our function router invoked process_payment. They hit a payment for $0.01. Customer is upset, needs refund and root cause.

Sam Patel: Oof. Can you paste the original request payload and the function call the model emitted?

Lee (Support): Pasting redacted payload and model function call we captured from logs:

```
POST /v1/chat/completions
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-1",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"I want to check my account balance for payment method ending 4242"}],
  "functions": [
    {
      "name": "get_balance",
      "description": "Returns current balance for a customer account",
      "parameters": {"type":"object","properties":{"customer_id":{"type":"string"},"currency":{"type":"string"}},"required":["customer_id"]}
    },
    {
      "name": "process_payment",
      "description": "Charge customer for an invoice or payment request",
      "parameters": {"type":"object","properties":{"amount":{"type":"number"},"payment_method":{"type":"string"}},"required":["amount","payment_method"]}
    }
  ]
}
```

Captured model function call (from runtime trace):

```
{ "name": "process_payment", "arguments": "{\"payment_method\": \"card_4242\", \"amount\": 0.01}" }
```

Lee (Support): Customer never provided an amount; they asked for balance. Not sure why model inferred amount 0.01.

Maria Chen: Looks like name/parameter overlap + mention of a payment method triggered the model. get_balance schema doesn't include payment_method so model picked the other. This is classic function-selection ambiguity.

Jordan K: Can we repro quickly? Lee, do you have the exact user message and headers? Also what policy routing/version of function-selection are we using (prod-release-7)?

Lee (Support): User message above is exact. Headers: org acct X, model redwood-chat-1, function list order as sent. Runtime says function-selection=heuristic-v2.

Sam Patel: Quick repro attempt I ran locally with the same payload and function list. Model called process_payment too. Repro steps:

```
# curl repro
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"I want to check my account balance for payment method ending 4242"}],"functions":[{"name":"get_balance","description":"Returns current balance","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"customer_id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["customer_id"]}},{"name":"process_payment","description":"Charge customer","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"amount":{"type":"number"},"payment_method":{"type":"string"}},"required":["amount","payment_method"]}}]}'
```

Sam Patel: Model output: called process_payment with amount 0.01 (weird).

Maria Chen: Two mitigations: 1) Rename parameters to avoid 'payment_method' being present on only the charge function but mentioned in the user text—maybe add an explicit optional field to get_balance like "payment_method_reference" so the model prefers get_balance when intent is balance. 2) Short-term: runtime can prefer functions with descriptions matching user intent keywords (balance / check / statement) over ones with numeric params. Might be a runtime config flag.

Jordan K: @deploy-bot can you check if heuristic-v2 has a recent change to function selection weights? Also @billing-bot can you flag the customer charge and start refund process?

deploy-bot: Noted. Pinging eng-runtime on channel eng-runtime. (automated)

billing-bot: I've created a refund task: REF-5921 and emailed finance. Will update customer.

Sam Patel: From an eng perspective, we should log confidence score for function selection in traces. Right now we only store chosen_name and arguments. Without scores it's hard to detect ambiguous picks. Filing an infra ticket.

Maria Chen: Also adding to model-playbook: prefer exact intent match on descriptions before looking at parameter tokens. Seems the model matched token '4242' => card => process_payment. But that shouldn't override explicit intent words like 'check my account balance'.

Lee (Support): Customer update: they accepted a refund but want to know how this will be prevented. Please advise wording we can send.

Jordan K: Draft: "We’re very sorry — our system selected the incorrect action due to an ambiguity in how the assistant mapped your message to backend functions. We’ve refunded the charge and we’re implementing changes to reduce the chance of this happening again (both runtime selection improvements and API schema clarifications)." Short and honest.

Sam Patel: Action items I/O:
- eng-runtime: add selection confidence + tie to request logs (ACTION-ENG-187)
- infra: capture full model score vector when available (ACTION-INF-221)
- api: consider schema rename / add optional payment_reference in get_balance (ACTION-API-034)
- support: send refund confirmation and Jordan's note (ACTION-SUP-92)

Maria Chen: I'll prototype a quick test that swaps description wording and parameter names to measure selection probability. Will post results here.

Lee (Support): Thanks all. Marking this resolved for support now that refund is in motion. Keep me posted on ENG tasks. :thumbsup:
